premises.text: There is no good enterprise knowledge base; knowledge sits in emails, IMs, and conversations
premises.evidence_span: It was siloed in emails, IMs, conversations. There was no good knowledge base.

premises.text: All content is organized around questions rather than segmented wiki documents
premises.evidence_span: unlike a wiki, which is all segmented into separate documents, all our content is organized around questions

premises.text: A voting mechanic lets colleagues endorse the best answers
premises.evidence_span: We have a voting mechanic that allows people to stand behind and endorse certain answers

premises.text: Enterprise-grade anonymity lets people ask the seemingly stupid questions that are the most common mistakes
premises.evidence_span: it allows for people to ask questions that maybe they thought was a little bit stupid but really are important because these are the most common mistakes that are made over and over again

premises.text: A fast, powerful search engine retrieves previous answers
premises.evidence_span: very fast, very powerful search engine that allows people to find previous answers to questions that they have already

premises.text: Users can ask and answer directly by email, with listserv content extracted into the searchable index and questions routed to the best candidates
premises.evidence_span: we allow people to ask questions directly by email, answer them directly by replying to an email

value.text: Employees at large companies share knowledge and turn to Opsy first when looking for answers
value.evidence_span: Opsy's mission is to help people at companies share knowledge.

causal_links.evidence_span: not being able to know what other people already knew
the power of this site is magnified when other people come on and answer questions
put them in our searchable index

notes: Feature-level reading: the speaker gives each mechanic (voting, anonymity, search) its own enterprise rationale, so they are coded as separate premises here; corporate-email verification is treated as an onboarding detail of the platform rather than its own premise. Singleton D1 (the need) and singleton D3 (the email integration track) each name an independently revisable module. The 'first place people turn' goal is treated as aspiration and not coded as a premise (v1.3.2 clarification 4). Investors and waitlist excluded.
